subject.broker: Azure Event Hubs Standard, Kafka endpoint

result: 15 min from a laptop, 3,000 events/s with 29,938/s mean for 2 min (peak 31,195/s), Kafka only: sent 5,934,943 with 0 errors, landed 5,935,273 (330 more: extra copies of sent events; no event_id more than twice); 225 STREAMING UPDATE commits 1-8 s apart (p50 4 s) and 15 OPTIMIZE; freshness p50 3.9 s / p90 5.3 s (before 4.6, during 5.1, after 3.7 s p50); max 29.7 s in the first 2 minutes, 11.1 s during the burst

setup.producer_host: laptop (macOS), over the internet to Event Hubs in centralus
setup.runtime: Lakeflow runtime: DBR 19.x, channel PREVIEW, image dlt:19.12.6 build 20261023, Azure centralus
setup.probe: serverless SQL warehouse, Small, 1 cluster; current_timestamp() minus the newest event time, every 2 s
setup.tool: lfc-kafka-freshness-test eventhubs.sh, connection.sh, pipeline.sh; zerobus-sdk-freshness-test producer.py, freshness_probe.py, report.py

notes: Compare 2026-10-29-lfc-kafka-freshness (producer a Databricks job in the same region, also writing Zerobus: burst mean 20,828/s). producer.py's run file doesn't count the duplicates it sends on purpose, so lost events can't be ruled out from the counts alone.
